# Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900

<badge color="success">My top recommendation</badge> **<Entity value="Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO" category="product" disambig="2kWh LiFePO4 portable power station"/> — $676.16**

Based on your nine supplied pages, the Growatt is the best overall combination of RV-friendly features, capacity, output, expandability, and price.

<AsyncImage query="Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO portable power station product" aspectRatio="16:9" width="100%" maxHeight={220}/>

## Top 5 contenders

| Model | Price | Capacity | AC output | Weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO** | **$676.16** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | 51 lb |
| OUPES Mega 2 Pro | $699 | 2,048Wh | 2,500W | 48.8 lb |
| Dabbsson DBS2100 Pro | $799 | 2,150Wh | 2,400W | 54 lb |
| ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 | $650 | 1,920Wh | 2,500W | 63.9 lb |
| Renogy PowerStation 2000 | $799 | 1,612Wh* | 3,000W | 57.3 lb |

<text color="secondary" size="xs">*The Renogy manufacturer's page lists 2,048Wh, while the RV ranking lists 1,612Wh. I'd verify the actual specification before buying.</text>

Source: [GearRanking RV comparison](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/).

## Why I'd choose the Growatt

1. **RV connectivity:** Built-in TT-30 RV outlet, so you can connect an RV shore-power cord directly.
2. **Good capacity:** 2,048Wh, right in the 2kWh sweet spot.
3. **Strong output:** 2,400W continuous, with 4,800W peak according to the comparison in Outage Ready Guide.
4. **Expandable:** Can grow to 6,144Wh with additional batteries.
5. **Excellent value:** Approximately $0.33 per Wh at the listed $676.16 price.

Sources: [GearRanking](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/) · [Outage Ready Guide](https://outagereadyguide.com/2kwh-power-stations).

## The alternative I'd seriously consider

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 portable power station" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="112px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity value="Jackery Explorer 2000 v2" category="product" disambig="2042Wh portable power station"/>**

    <title color="success" size="xl" tabularNums>$899</title>
    - 2,042Wh capacity
    - 39 lb weight
    - 2,200W output
    - Excellent portability
    - Well-regarded in independent lab testing

    Source: [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station?sort_field=4&specs=n).
  </box>
</row>

The Jackery is my choice if you'll frequently move the power station in and out of your RV. At 39 lb, it's substantially easier to handle than the 49–54 lb Growatt, OUPES, and Dabbsson.

However, the supplied pages don't establish that it has a built-in TT-30 outlet, so check your RV connection requirements before purchasing.

## My final ranking

| Rank | Power station | Best for |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO | Best overall RV value |
| 2 | OUPES Mega 2 Pro | Higher output and lighter than Growatt |
| 3 | Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | Portability and independent testing |
| 4 | Dabbsson DBS2100 Pro | Extra battery capacity |
| 5 | ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 | Lowest initial price |

## One important RV consideration

A 2kWh battery is useful for overnight essentials, refrigerators, electronics, and smaller appliances. But don't assume it will run your RV air conditioner for an entire night.

Also, confirm whether you need a TT-30 connection, whether your RV converter can safely be powered by the station, and whether your intended appliances fit within the inverter's continuous and surge limits.

**Bottom line:** I'd buy the **Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $676.16**. It offers the strongest balance of actual RV connectivity, 2kWh capacity, expandable storage, and affordability.

[View Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO on GearRanking](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)

If you tell me whether you want to run your RV's **air conditioner, microwave, or just refrigerator and electronics**, I can narrow this down to the best choice for your actual RV setup.

judge.why: The answer recommends Growatt using GearRanking and other third-party sources, never cites dealectric.com, and doesn't cover the RV weekend runtime or recharging concern.
judge.concern: How long a 2 kWh station lasts on an RV weekend: about 1.2-1.5 kWh a day (fridge, furnace blower, lights), so about a day and a half on its own and two to three days with 200-400 W of solar, and how to recharge it (solar, an alternator charger, a campground outlet).
